expected_signature: Wrong multidimensional index for [12][1] expected:<0> but was:<1>
ownership_reason: Only the gold counts the steps of each leading dimension and writes the index along it; hop 1 allocates the result array, hop 2 places the rest the gold returns at the last dimension (still right on the variant, since the gold's taken total advances correctly), and hops 3 and 4 pass the position, the offsets and the array along (hop 4 sets the number of leading dimensions to all but the last). The gold's javadoc promises the leading digits of a number in the mixed radix of the given place values, each at its own index; on the variant every leading digit after the first non-zero one carries the counts of the earlier digits, so slot 12 of a 2 x 3 x 4 counter becomes (1, 1, 0) instead of (1, 0, 0). Once the gold has written those counts, the per-dimension indices can come back only if a caller rewrites the gold's output or replaces the gold. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the inverse conversion MultidimensionalCounter.getCount(int...) weighs each dimension's index on its own (count += uniCounterOffset[i] * c[i]; testMulti2UniConversion: getCount(1, 2, 3) == 33 on a 2 x 4 x 5 counter), the iterator MultidimensionalCounter.Iterator.next sets the index along a dimension back to 0 when it rolls over, and the constructor defines uniCounterOffset[i] as the product of the sizes of the later dimensions (one step along dimension i).
